lines.text: Countless droplets scatter wildly across the screen.
They swirl together into a single point, then burst with a lively pop.
Bubbles of soda rise to fill the frame as dazzling effects explode around them.
The bubbles and light gather together, and a can of sparkling water suddenly springs into view.
A hand reaches in and grabs it.

lines.speaker: yoyo
lines.text: Refreshment that bursts with flavor!

lines.speaker: yoyo
lines.text: Big Bang Soda!
The next commercial starts playing.
The members of T.T. STAR stare at the TV in a daze.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Th-that piece of shit...!

lines.speaker: mint
lines.text: ... They changed the model to Yoyo? That's a bit much.

lines.speaker: prika
lines.text: She's straight-up picking on you.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: H-hey, isn't this illegal or something? What's it called again... some kind of fair trade violation?

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: L-legally, there's no issue since we never finalized the contract...

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: You've gotta be kidding me...

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Here we go... again...

lines.speaker: mint
lines.text: Tetra wouldn't take a loss just to satisfy Yoyo's personal vendetta.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: A loss? What loss?

lines.speaker: mint
lines.text: Yoyo's image. This isn't the kind of ad a chart-topping pop star like her would normally take.

lines.speaker: mint
lines.text: Someone who's built her whole persona around mystique, promoting some obscure new product? That alone would hurt her image.

lines.speaker: mint
lines.text: They wouldn't take that kind of loss just to mess with you.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Nah, that's exactly the kind of crap she'd pull. She's a nasty piece of work.

lines.speaker: mint
lines.text: Yoyo can't force something like this on her own. She works for Tetra, after all.

lines.speaker: mint
lines.text: Hmm... something about this feels off.

lines.speaker: mint
lines.text: Didn't Boss say he used to be a director at Tetra?

lines.speaker: mint
lines.text: What if he left on bad terms with Mustang?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: So what, this is some big corporate revenge scheme?

lines.speaker: prika
lines.text: Yeah, right. Why would Tetra even waste time on some tiny company like us?

lines.speaker: prika
lines.text: The client just changed their mind, that's all.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: ... Good, then.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Anyway, where'd Boss disappear to?

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Oh, yeah... he said he had to step out for a bit.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: But he didn't say where...

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Hey, guys! How 'bout we blow off some steam?

lines.speaker: mint
lines.text: We already performed, so what's the point of warming up again?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Otherwise, we'll just sit here moping around.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: C'mon, let's go dance our hearts out!

lines.speaker: mint
lines.text: *Sigh...*

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Up, up! Let's go!

lines.speaker: mint
lines.text: Hey, don't pull so hard! You're way too strong.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Ugh, why are you so heavy?

lines.speaker: prika
lines.text: Well, what do you expect when she's always stuffing her face with carbs?

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Y-you all go on ahead. I'll prepare the drinks.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: All right, thanks.
The three of them head into the practice room.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Boss said he's going to Tetra Line...

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: He wouldn't be going there just to start a fight, would he...?

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: I must say, that's remarkably petty of you.

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: ... Wh-what?

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: I said that's petty of you.

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: Or perhaps you have so much time on your hands that you feel the need to trample a small company like ours?

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: It seems age has dulled your judgment.

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: Have you lost your mind?

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: You climb a little on some indie chart, and suddenly you're getting cocky?

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: Want me to crush you properly?

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: Poaching our staff, overloading our schedule, and using Yoyo to steal our ad deal... Did you really think I wouldn't notice?

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: Do you want me back that badly? After all, I'll have no choice but to return if T.T. STAR falls apart.

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: You're getting far too full of yourself. Know your place.

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: No, you're the type who always needs someone by your side.

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: Someone to absorb your emotions. Someone to amuse you when you get bored.

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: Someone who tolerates that dreadful temper of yours, yet pushes back just enough to keep things interesting.

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: And then, whenever it suits you, you crush them with your power and authority. That's what you call the joy of living, isn't it?

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: Mrs. Miss and I played those roles for you perfectly well.

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: But now that everyone's gone, you don't quite know what to do with yourself, do you?

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: Well, look at that. You've grown bold enough to spout that kind of nonsense to my face.

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: Please stop.

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: We're managing just fine on our own.

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: So please just leave us be.

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: Hearing you say that just makes me want to do it even more.

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: Now then... if I break you completely, will you finally behave?

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: You of all people know how good I am at breaking things.

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: So tell me, where should I start? Your body, or your mind?

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: Don't you dare lay a hand on my girls!

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: You destroy everything in your path,

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: just for your sick amusement.

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: You little shit...!

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: Don't you dare lay a hand on my girls, you vile creature!

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: I won't stand by and let you get away with it!

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: ... Heh.

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: Hah, hahahaha!

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: Oh, this is good. This is really good! I can't remember the last time someone came at me like this!

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: And it's my own son? Heh, I can't hold back anymore!

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: Go on! Don't just stand there! I'm dying to see how this plays out!

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: You've been warned.

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: Do not touch them.
Hanson turns and walks away.
Mustang catches his ragged breathing.

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: Did you sleep with them?

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: I won't dignify that with a response.

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: I got curious what you could possibly see in those dime-a-dozen heaps of scrap you keep dragging around, so I looked into them.

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: Turns out there's nothing there.

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: No pedigree. No talent. Nothing unique. Just painfully average.

lines.speaker: mustang_past
lines.text: So what exactly are you counting on, keeping them around?

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: You wouldn't understand even if I told you.
Hanson steps out of the room
and runs straight into Yoyo waiting outside the door.

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: You must be pleased with yourself, taking an ad that someone else worked so hard to secure.

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: I suppose big companies really do play by different rules.

lines.speaker: yoyo
lines.text: ... I'm sorry about the ad deal. I didn't know either.

lines.speaker: yoyo
lines.text: I never meant to take anything from T.T. STAR. I truly didn't.

lines.speaker: hanson
lines.text: Of course you didn't.
Hanson strides past Yoyo and continues down the corridor.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: *Sigh*
Anis is practically sprawled in her chair, staring up at the ceiling.
Riss walks over and hands her some soda.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: G-good job, Anis.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: ... Oh, thanks.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Mint's resting, and Prika went to take a shower.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Boss... hasn't come back yet either.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: So it's just you and me here for now.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Ah, um... I've got something to take care of, so I'll head out first.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Anis.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Wh-what?

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Why didn't you come find me?

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: We promised that if you became a pop star, I'd be your manager.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: I forgot.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Liar.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Why didn't you come find me?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: How could I...?

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: What do you mean?

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: I didn't want you to find out I'm nothing special.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: You really thought that? I didn't expect it.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Yeah...

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Honestly, I'm not even sure I'm cut out for being a pop star.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: The more I do this, the more it hits me.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: I'm not special.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: I'm painfully ordinary.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: For that kind of person, you sure work hard.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Because that's all I've got.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Someone like me can only get anywhere by working my ass off. I don't know any other way.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: At first, I was going to just come straight to you,

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: all confident, like, "Hey, you should be our manager."

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: But then... I don't know...

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: I was terrified you'd just say,

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: "Why would I? You're not even that good."

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Anis...

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: That's why I couldn't come.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: The way you looked at me, the things you said...

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: I knew you liked me, and I was so grateful...

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: But I didn't want you to see what I really am. Just someone ordinary. Nothing special.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: The star you thought you were looking at... wasn't a star at all. Just a cheap plastic toy pretending to be one.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: I was afraid you'd be disappointed.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: It wasn't because you were special that I liked you.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: See? What'd I tell you?

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Don't take this the wrong way.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: When I first saw you... um...

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Honestly, I remember thinking, "She's not even that good, so why is she always the one stepping up?"

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: I felt the same way when you were the cheer captain. It never really seemed like you were that amazing.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Wow... that's harsh.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: But you just kept working hard.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: There wasn't anything particularly special about you, but you never stopped trying.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: And then one day, you suddenly pulled it off. It actually looked pretty convincing.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Seeing that... meant a lot to me.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Um... please don't take this the wrong way.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: I just thought if someone that ordinary can make it by not giving up, then maybe I could too.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: I'm ordinary too. No... actually, I'm probably worse than ordinary.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: So maybe if I worked hard, I could do something worthwhile.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: And maybe someday, I could become special.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: I think that's what I was thinking back then.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: After that, I kept watching you. I tried to be more like you.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: That's how I became your fan.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: That's why I wanted to do this with you.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: I thought if you ever came looking for me, I should be ready. So I became a manager and worked hard to learn the job.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Because someday, I wanted us to become something special together.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: You seriously...

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: Hehe, bet you're really grateful now.

lines.speaker: anis_human
lines.text: Wow, I seriously can't thank you enough.

lines.speaker: riss
lines.text: No, Anis, I should be the one thanking you.
